channel.title: Beben Design Blog
channel.description: Notes from the workshop at Beben Design: design decisions, engineering trade-offs, and the tools I ship, written from inside real projects.

item.title: What foundational SEO gets you, and what it doesn't
item.description: The SEO work worth doing at launch, the parts that are a separate job, and how to tell the difference in a quote.

item.title: Your domain and email: what you should own, and why
item.description: The accounts that should be in your name before a website project starts, and the handover checklist that stops a supplier from holding your business hostage.

item.title: Before you redesign: what to check first
item.description: A redesign is cheaper when you know what is actually broken. The checks worth doing before you brief anyone, and what to keep.

item.title: How to brief a designer in one page
item.description: The five things a designer needs before a useful reply, and the one-page brief I use to turn a vague idea into a scoped project.

item.title: What a website actually costs, and what to check in a quote
item.description: A practical way to read a website quote, compare line items, and spot the costs that get left out. Prices in USD, from $250.

item.title: Beben Arcade - twenty-three games that work with the wifi off
item.description: Beben Arcade is a pocket arcade of tiny games. No ads, no account, works offline, and plays on anything with a browser.

item.title: Codex - an offline library that answers in milliseconds
item.description: I had 180GB of offline archives that worked and were almost unusable. Codex rebuilds them into plain SQLite, 25x smaller, searchable in single-digit milliseconds, readable by any language. What it is, why it exists, and how it was built.

item.title: Building Sprite - a chat widget with two brains
item.description: How I built a zero-dependency site guide that answers from an LLM when it can and from a pattern engine when it can't, on a static site with no backend and no keys in the repo.

item.title: Rev Log - why the data format is the product
item.description: My open source motorcycle telemetry project ships a ride-data format before it ships hardware. The reasoning behind that order, and what it changes about everything else.

item.title: A tool you can download and own
item.description: My QR code generator is one HTML file that works offline forever. The engineering and the ethics of building tools people can take with them.
